headline: Austrian household power bills jump a third, a record
text:
# Austrian household power bills jump a third, a record

Europe's energy numbers dominate today: record household electricity rises in Austria and Luxembourg, the UK's last coal all but gone, and Greek renewables past 60%.

## Today in the data

### Austrian bills at a record high
[Household electricity, EUR per kWh, all taxes in](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
Austria paid €0.3272 per kWh in H2 2025 (energy-household-eu), 34.3% above H2 2024 and the biggest yearly rise since 2008. Luxembourg moved almost in step, €0.2665 and +31.7%. Both are taxes-included prices, so an expiring levy holiday moves the line as much as wholesale power does — worth checking against national tax schedules.

### US chip-price index still climbing
[US chip prices and chip output, year on year](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
Factory-gate prices for computer and electronic products rose 12.9% in the year to Aug 2026 (us-ppi-sectors), against a usual +0.63%. Semiconductor output was up 11.9% in Jul 2026 (us-chips), so prices and volumes are rising together — unusual for this sector. The PPI is not seasonally adjusted and the volume index is quality-adjusted, so the two are not like for like.

### Austrian pharma output halves
[Austrian pharma output against chemicals and the EU](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
Austria's pharma index stood at 160.4 in Jul 2026 (eu-ipi-sectors, 2021=100), 45.7% below Jul 2025 and the sharpest fall since 2011. Note the comparison base: a year earlier the index was near 295, a spike the EU27 line (149.6 in Jun 2026) never showed. Small-country pharma series are batch-driven and heavily revised.

### Britain's last coal year
[UK electricity generation by source, TWh](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
UK coal generation was 0.33 TWh in 2025 (electricity-mix), down 82.6% on 2024 and the sharpest fall in a record starting in 1921. Wind, at 85.84 TWh, is now within striking distance of gas at 90.91 TWh. The last year is often Ember's provisional figure, so treat 2025 as subject to revision.

### Estonia's new-car market halves
[New car registrations in Estonia by fuel](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
Estonia registered 13,141 new cars in 2025 (eu-car-registrations), 49% fewer than 2024, with diesel down 70.4% to 1,738. Battery-electric registrations, at 872, did not fill the gap: this is a market shrinking, not switching. A registration tax introduced in the period is worth checking against; the series only starts in 2013.

### Egyptian FDI falls back to normal
[Egypt: foreign direct investment, net inflows](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
Egypt took in $15.5bn of net FDI in 2025 (macro-external), $31.1bn less than in 2024 and the sharpest fall since 1971. The chart shows 2024 as the outlier, not 2025: one very large inflow year sets up the base effect. World Bank data lag one to two years and annual figures are revised.

### Greece past sixty percent renewable
[Greece: renewables as a share of electricity](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
Greece's renewable share of electricity reached 60.9% in 2025 (eu-renewables-share), up 9.65 points in a year against a usual 2.17. The step in the last two points is larger than anything since 2005. This is the Directive's accounting definition, not raw generation, so it differs from Ember's figures.

## Forecasts

### US chip prices grind higher into November
[us-ppi-sectors:computer_electronic forecast](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
The index was 120.048 in Aug 2026 (us-ppi-sectors). Holt-Winters additive, period 12, puts Nov 2026 at 122.33 with a 95% band of 120.90 to 123.77. In-sample fit is tight: MAPE 0.28%, residual sd 0.42. The band says only that, if the recent pattern holds, four in five months' outcomes land inside it. A tariff change or a break in the memory-chip cycle would put the November print outside.

### Austrian pharma output roughly flat
[eu-ipi-sectors:AT|C21 forecast](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
The index was 160.4 in Jul 2026 (eu-ipi-sectors). The same method gives 165.7 for Oct 2026, but with a band from 124.7 to 206.8: residual sd is 12.1 and MAPE 5.0%, so this series is barely forecastable at three months. The band is wide because past months swing this much. The next Eurostat release, due for August, plus revisions to the 2025 spike, could move the level well outside it.

### Austrian bills settle near today's level
[energy-household-eu:AT forecast](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
The last observation is €0.3272 per kWh in H2 2025 (energy-household-eu). Holt-Winters, period 2, gives €0.3249 for H2 2026, band €0.2904 to €0.3594, with MAPE 3.3%. This is a price shaped by taxes, levies and network tariffs, so the projection extrapolates past administrative decisions rather than a market. Any new levy, or the return of a subsidy, puts the outcome outside the band.

## Correlations
- **Austria vs Luxembourg household electricity** (yoy, 2008-S2 to 2025-S2, n=35): r = 0.61 at lag −1 and 0.53 at lag 0, both clear the 0.36 band. Their bills move together within a half-year, consistent with common wholesale and levy timing; the lag-4 peak (r = 0.64) is the largest of nine and should be treated as a hypothesis.
- **US semiconductor output vs computer-electronic PPI** (yoy, 2012-01 to 2026-07, n=175): r = 0.01 at lag 0, peak |r| = 0.14, not distinguishable from zero at any lag within ±12 months. Today's simultaneous jump in both is not a stable relationship in this record.

## What to watch
- **eu-ipi-sectors** (last 2026-07): the August print settles whether Austria's pharma collapse is a base effect or a level shift.
- **us-ppi-sectors** (last 2026-08): next month says if the 12.9% chip-price rise is still accelerating.
- **eu-ppi-sectors** and **eu-esi** (last 2026-08): European producer prices and sentiment for September.
- **cpi-eu** and **eu-hicp** (last 2026-07): whether household energy costs are showing up in headline inflation.
- **energy-household-eu**: H1 2026 prices will test whether Austria's record rise persists.

## Sources
- energy-household-eu — Eurostat nrg_pc_204, household band DC, taxes included; last 2025-S2.
- us-ppi-sectors — BLS producer price indexes by NAICS via FRED, NSA; last 2026-08.
- us-chips — Federal Reserve industrial production via FRED (NAICS 3344, 334); last 2026-07.
- eu-ipi-sectors — Eurostat sts_inpr_m, 2021=100, adjusted; last 2026-07.
- electricity-mix — Ember Yearly Electricity Data and Energy Institute via Our World in Data; last 2025.
- eu-car-registrations — Eurostat road_eqr_carpda; last 2025.
- macro-external — World Bank World Development Indicators; last 2025.
- eu-renewables-share — Eurostat nrg_ind_ren; last 2025.
